jp: 空[そら]が暗[くら]くて、今[いま]にも雨[あめ]が{降[ふ]りそうです|pt-sou-look}。
en: The sky is dark, and it looks like it is going to rain any moment now.
why: Verb stem + そう describes how something looks right now, here a coming rain.

jp: このケーキはクリームがたっぷりで、とても{おいしそうです|pt-sou-look}。
en: This cake is piled with cream and looks very delicious.
why: Adjective stem + そう gives an impression from appearance, before you taste it.

jp: 彼女[かのじょ]は{うれしそうな|pt-sou-look}顔[かお]でプレゼントを開[あ]けました。
en: She opened the present with a happy-looking face.
why: Before a noun, stem + そうな means 'looking happy' from the outside.

jp: おばあさんが{重[おも]そうな|pt-sou-look}荷物[にもつ]を持[も]って階段[かいだん]を上[のぼ]っています。
en: An old woman is climbing the stairs carrying luggage that looks heavy.
why: 重い drops い and takes そうな to describe how the luggage looks.

jp: 木[き]の上[うえ]の猫[ねこ]が今[いま]にも{落[お]ちそうです|pt-sou-look}。
en: The cat up in the tree looks as if it is about to fall.
why: 今にも plus verb stem + そう expresses something that looks about to happen.

jp: 顔色[かおいろ]が悪[わる]くて、田中[たなか]さんは具合[ぐあい]が{悪[わる]そうです|pt-sou-look}。
en: Mr. Tanaka looks unwell; his complexion is bad.
why: The impression comes from what you can see (his face), so stem + そう.

jp: 見[み]ただけでは、この問題[もんだい]は{簡単[かんたん]そうです|pt-sou-look}が、実[じつ]は難[むずか]しいです。
en: Just looking at it, this problem looks easy, but it is actually hard.
d: 簡単[かんたん]ではありません
簡単[かんたん]になりました
why: 見ただけでは marks a first impression, which is what そう (appearance) expresses.

jp: 子[こ]どもたちは公園[こうえん]で{楽[たの]しそうに|pt-sou-look}遊[あそ]んでいます。
en: The children are playing in the park looking as if they are having fun.
why: Stem + そうに modifies the verb: they play in a way that looks fun.

jp: 窓[まど]から見[み]ると、外[そと]は雪[ゆき]が降[ふ]っていて{寒[さむ]そうです|pt-sou-look}。
en: Looking from the window, it is snowing outside and it looks cold.
why: An impression taken from the view through the window is stem + そう.

jp: この橋[はし]は古[ふる]くて、今[いま]にも{壊[こわ]れそうです|pt-sou-look}。
en: This bridge is old and looks like it will collapse any moment.
d: 壊[こわ]れないはずです
why: Something visibly about to happen takes verb stem + そう.

jp: {眠[ねむ]そうな|pt-sou-look}顔[かお]をしていますね。昨夜[ゆうべ]は遅[おそ]かったんですか。
en: You look sleepy. Was last night a late one?
why: The speaker judges from the face, so 眠い becomes 眠そうな before 顔.

jp: 湯気[ゆげ]が出[で]ていて、スープが{熱[あつ]そうです|pt-sou-look}から、ゆっくり飲[の]んでください。
en: Steam is rising and the soup looks hot, so please drink it slowly.
why: The steam is visible evidence, giving an appearance judgement with そう.

jp: 空[そら]を見[み]ると、雨[あめ]は{やみそうにありません|pt-sou-look}。
en: Looking at the sky, it doesn't look as if the rain will stop.
why: Stem + そうにありません says it does not look as if something will happen.

jp: 机[つくえ]の上[うえ]に書類[しょるい]がいっぱいで、{忙[いそが]しそうですね|pt-sou-look}。
en: Your desk is full of papers; you look busy.
d: 忙[いそが]しいそうですね
忙[いそが]しかったですね
忙[いそが]しくないですね
why: The comment is based on what the speaker sees on the desk, so stem + そう.

jp: 店[みせ]で手[て]に取[と]って見[み]ると、このカバンは丈夫[じょうぶ]で{長[なが]く使[つか]えそうです|pt-sou-look}。
en: Picking it up in the shop, this bag is sturdy and looks like it can be used for a long time.
d: 長[なが]く使[つか]えるそうです
長[なが]く使[つか]いました
長[なが]く使[つか]いたいです
why: The judgement comes from handling the bag; use stem + そう.

jp: テストの結果[けっか]が悪[わる]くて、妹[いもうと]は今[いま]にも{泣[な]きそうです|pt-sou-look}。
en: My little sister got a bad test result and looks about to cry.
why: 今にも with a verb stem + そう shows a state that looks about to burst out.

jp: 見[み]た目[め]は{辛[から]そうです|pt-sou-look}が、食[た]べてみると甘[あま]かったです。
en: It looks spicy, but when I tried it, it was sweet.
d: 辛[から]くなかったです
why: 見た目は points to the appearance only, which is what そう describes.

jp: 窓[まど]の外[そと]を見[み]ると、明日[あした]は{晴[は]れそうです|pt-sou-look}。
en: Looking out of the window, it looks like tomorrow will be fine.
d: 晴[は]れてしまいました
why: A forecast from what you see outside uses verb stem + そう.

jp: この仕事[しごと]は今日[きょう]中[じゅう]に{終[お]わりそうにありません|pt-sou-look}。
en: It doesn't look as if this work will be finished today.
why: The speaker judges from the situation; stem + そうにありません is the negative.

jp: 上着[うわぎ]のボタンが今[いま]にも{取[と]れそうです|pt-sou-look}よ。
en: The button on your jacket looks like it will come off any moment.
why: A visible, imminent change takes verb stem + そう.

jp: 彼女[かのじょ]は{さびしそうに|pt-sou-look}一人[ひとり]でお茶[ちゃ]を飲[の]んでいました。
en: She was drinking tea alone, looking lonely.
why: Stem + そうに describes the way she looked while drinking tea.

jp: 店[みせ]で見[み]ると、この靴[くつ]は{歩[ある]きやすそうです|pt-sou-look}ね。
en: Looking at it in the shop, these shoes look easy to walk in.
d: 歩[ある]きやすいそうです
歩[ある]きやすかったです
why: Their look suggests comfort, so 歩きやすい becomes 歩きやすそう.

jp: 先生[せんせい]に聞[き]かなくても、この問題[もんだい]は私[わたし]にも{できそうです|pt-sou-look}。
en: Even without asking the teacher, this problem looks like something I can do too.
why: Looking at the problem, the speaker senses it is possible: できそう.

jp: 風[かぜ]が強[つよ]くなってきて、台風[たいふう]が{来[き]そうです|pt-sou-look}。
en: The wind is getting stronger, and a typhoon looks like it is coming.
why: Signs you can see now (the rising wind) call for stem + そう.

jp: 並[なら]んで笑[わら]っているあの二人[ふたり]は、仲[なか]が{よさそうです|pt-sou-look}ね。
en: Those two laughing side by side look close.
why: いい/よい becomes よさそう in the appearance form; it is judged by looking.

jp: 写真[しゃしん]で見[み]ると、この部屋[へや]は{広[ひろ]そうです|pt-sou-look}ね。
en: Judging from the photo, this room looks spacious.
why: A photo gives a visual impression, so 広い becomes 広そう.

jp: 見[み]たところ、これは一人[ひとり]では{持[も]てなさそうです|pt-sou-look}。
en: From the look of it, I don't think I can carry this by myself.
why: 見たところ shows a judgement from appearance; negative potential gives 持てなさそう.

jp: 今日[きょう]は忙[いそが]しくて、昼[ひる]ご飯[はん]を食[た]べる時間[じかん]が{なさそうです|pt-sou-look}。
en: Today is busy, and it looks as if I won't have time to eat lunch.
why: ない becomes なさそう in the appearance form: it looks like there is none.

jp: あの店[みせ]は人[ひと]が多[おお]くて、入[はい]るのに時間[じかん]が{かかりそうです|pt-sou-look}。
en: That shop is crowded, so getting in looks like it will take a while.
why: From the crowd you can see, you predict it: verb stem + そう.

jp: 駅[えき]で{親切[しんせつ]そうな|pt-sou-look}人[ひと]に道[みち]を聞[き]きました。
en: At the station I asked a kind-looking person the way.
d: 親切[しんせつ]ではない
親切[しんせつ]なはずの
why: A na-adjective drops な and adds そうな before a noun to describe appearance.

jp: 子[こ]どもは{元気[げんき]そうに|pt-sou-look}走[はし]っています。
en: The child is running along looking full of energy.
why: Stem + そうに turns 元気 into 'looking energetic' for the verb.

jp: ガラスのケースに入[はい]った、あの時計[とけい]は{高[たか]そうです|pt-sou-look}ね。
en: That watch in the glass case looks expensive.
why: The impression comes from looking at it; 高い becomes 高そう.

jp: 点差[てんさ]が大[おお]きくて、この試合[しあい]は{負[ま]けそうです|pt-sou-look}。
en: We are far behind on points, and it looks like we will lose this match.
why: The score you can see leads to a prediction: verb stem + そう.

jp: デザートを見[み]て、妹[いもうと]は{食[た]べたそうに|pt-sou-look}していました。
en: Looking at the dessert, my little sister looked as if she wanted to eat it.
why: 〜たい drops い before そう to show that someone looks as if they want to.

jp: 彼[かれ]は私[わたし]に{何[なに]か話[はな]したそうな|pt-sou-look}顔[かお]をしていました。
en: He had a face that looked as if he wanted to tell me something.
d: 何[なに]か話[はな]したくない
何[なに]か話[はな]したあとの
何[なに]か話[はな]すための
why: 話したい becomes 話したそう; before 顔 it takes な.

jp: 図書館[としょかん]に入[はい]ると、ここは{勉強[べんきょう]しやすそうです|pt-sou-look}。
en: Stepping into the library, I see this place looks easy to study in.
d: 勉強[べんきょう]しやすいそうです
勉強[べんきょう]しにくいです
勉強[べんきょう]しやすかったです
why: First impression on entering: 〜やすい becomes 〜やすそう.

jp: 夜[よる]の道[みち]は暗[くら]くて、一人[ひとり]で歩[ある]くのは{危[あぶ]なそうです|pt-sou-look}。
en: The road at night is dark, and walking it alone looks dangerous.
why: 危ない becomes 危なそう (not 危ないそう) in the appearance form.

jp: 夏[なつ]なのにコートを着[き]ている人[ひと]を見[み]て、母[はは]は「あの人[ひと]、{暑[あつ]そうだ|pt-sou-look}ね」と言[い]いました。
en: Seeing a person wearing a coat in summer, my mother said, "That person looks hot."
why: She speaks from what she sees, so 暑い becomes 暑そうだ.

jp: 荷物[にもつ]が多[おお]くて、このカバンには{入[はい]りそうにありません|pt-sou-look}。
en: There is a lot of luggage, and it doesn't look like it will fit in this bag.
d: 入[はい]りたくありません
why: Judging by the amount, the speaker says it does not look like it will fit.

jp: 風邪[かぜ]をひいたのか、娘[むすめ]は{つらそうに|pt-sou-look}せきをしています。
en: My daughter may have caught a cold; she is coughing and looks as if it hurts.
why: Stem + そうに describes how the coughing looks to the speaker.

jp: 雪[ゆき]で道[みち]が凍[こお]っていて、歩[ある]くと{滑[すべ]りそうです|pt-sou-look}。
en: The road is frozen with snow, and when I walk it looks like I will slip.
d: 滑[すべ]らないはずです
why: A risk you can see right now takes verb stem + そう.
